raw_response:
Alright, let me think about this year's planning.

---

I'm getting older now, 53, and my knees aren't what they used to be. But I've been doing this land for thirty years so I mostly know what works and what doesn't. My old man helps, and our oldest son comes back from the city for busy times like wheat harvest. The two younger ones have steady factory work so they send money but don't help in the fields much anymore.

We have 60 mu total. Same as last year, I'll put 40 mu in wheat-maize like always — that's the steady one, two harvests a year, and we keep some grain for ourselves too. The other 20 mu I'll keep in cotton. Cotton is more trouble and the price goes up and down, but when it's good it brings real money, and anyway the land out there isn't so good for wheat. My second sister's husband grows cotton too, and we usually do the same things around the same time.

**Wheat (40 mu).** I'll plant in early October like always, once the maize is off and the ground is turned. Seed I buy from the co-op shop, the common variety everyone uses — about a bag and a half per mu, maybe 15 kilos. No need for anything fancy, my neighbors all plant the same kind and it does fine.

For fertilizer, same as every year — one bag of compound (50 kg) per mu mixed in before planting, that gives it a good start. Then when the wheat turns green again in spring, around the time the swallows come back, I'll spread half a bag of urea on top. If it looks yellow I might add a little more, but usually half a bag is enough. My husband says we could use less compound but I don't want to risk it — if the wheat doesn't fill out the head, the whole year is bad. Better to put a little extra than not enough.

Water — the well is working alright. I'll water it once before winter so the roots don't dry out, once again when it greens up in spring, once at jointing when the stems are getting tall, and once more when the grain is filling. So four times. Pumping costs money, but wheat here needs water, no way around it. If it rains good in May I might skip the last one.

For bugs and weeds — I'll spray the weed killer in early spring, the kind the shopkeeper recommends. If I see aphids at heading time I'll spray once, otherwise I don't bother.

Last year I got about 420 kg per mu. Year before was better, maybe 450. I'll hope for around 420 again.

**Maize (40 mu, after wheat).** Right after wheat harvest in June — we have maybe five or six days to get the maize in. We hire the combine for wheat and the planter-man comes right after with the maize seed. No time to plow properly, just plant straight into the stubble. That's how everyone does it now.

Seed is the hybrid kind, I buy a bag each year, can't save it. One bag of compound per mu at planting same as wheat, then when the maize is knee-high I'll spread some urea — maybe half a bag per mu. My neighbor says she uses less but her yields are a bit lower so I stick with what I know.

Water — depends on the summer rain. Usually I irrigate once when it's tasseling if it's been dry, maybe twice in a bad year. Last summer was wet so I only watered once.

Spray once for the corn borer in July. I usually get around 480 kg per mu.

**Cotton (20 mu).** Cotton is the hard one. My sister-in-law and I do ours around the same time, mid-late April when the soil is warm enough. We lay the plastic film and plant by hand, my husband does most of the film work, my sister comes over to help plant.

Seed I buy, about 2 kg per mu, the regular kind from the shop. Before planting I put one bag of compound down per mu. Then when it starts flowering in July I'll topdress a little urea, maybe a third of a bag per mu — cotton doesn't need as much as wheat or maize.

Water I give it once or twice — once at squaring and once at flowering if it's dry. Cotton doesn't like too much water, the old farmers say.

Spraying is where cotton costs money. Bollworms, aphids, red spider — I spray maybe four, five times through the summer. Plus the growth regulator to keep it from getting too tall. The shopkeeper mixes what I need.

The picking — that's all me and my husband and my older sister when she can come. No hired hands, too expensive. We pick three, four times from September through October. Last year I got about 240 kg of lint per mu. A decent year.

**Money.** I figured in my head roughly — about 20,000 for wheat, 17,000 for maize, maybe 8,000 for cotton. All told near 45,000 yuan for the inputs. I have most of it saved from last year's sale, and if short I borrow from my brother-in-law, not the bank. I keep some cash back in case the cotton spray gets expensive or the pump breaks.
